assumptions.description: Task-defined analytical design has 375 rows in each female=0/1 by age-band cell (25-39,40-54,55-69,70-79), 3000 total. Source demographic margins are contextual and are not imposed. Female is coded exactly as the task.
Conditional on each specified age band, integer ages are discrete uniform. This completion of the within-band age distribution is assumed, not identified by source age mean/SD.

BMI, fasting glucose, and HbA1c are mutually independent and independent of age and female in the selected analytical population. This factorization is an explicit unresolved-dependence completion chosen because E0 supplies no relationships. It is not an empirical zero-association finding and can be scientifically wrong. All requested adjusted associations are assumption-dependent.

The Jansen Table 1 BMI, fasting-glucose and HbA1c marginal location and dispersion are transported unchanged to every target sex/age stratum, treating the reported SD as individual dispersion. European ancestry, older-member GWAS selection, anemia exclusion, assay and plasma/serum differences, and undocumented hours fasted are not corrected. No verified transport invariance is claimed.

BMI follows a positive gamma law whose shape and scale are fixed by its chosen mean and SD. Distribution shape, skewness and all tails are assumptions; neither an observed BMI range nor a clinical plausibility cutoff is supplied. Very small and arbitrarily large positive values have mathematical support.

Glucose and HbA1c follow separately scaled beta laws. Glucose support (0,126) mg/dL enforces the task selection; the law is directly conditional on eligibility rather than a truncated unselected disease model. HbA1c support (0,100) percent is a broad modeling bound consistent with percentage notation, not a reported population cutoff or clinical reference interval. Beta shape, density and tails are assumed.

Use the directly published rounded HbA1c percent mean 5.6 and SD 0.3 as the single selected unit representation. IFCC values 38 and 3 convert to 5.62824 and 0.27444, respectively; they are redundant rounded representations, not independent data. No fitting to both is attempted. Glucose uses the supplied fixed 18.0 mg/dL per mmol/L conversion.

Rows are fictional adults conditional on all task eligibility, measurement-documentation and routing restrictions. The model does not generate diagnosis, fasting hours, pregnancy/lactation, anemia, medication use or anthropometry-documentation fields. Only the six permitted columns are returned. Source exclusions do not establish target anemia or medication exclusion.

Reported means and SDs are fixed construction inputs, with source estimator uncertainty not supplied and not inferred from SD or n. Seeds vary individual residual draws only. External-estimate uncertainty, factorization uncertainty, shape uncertainty and transport uncertainty are unresolved; repeated seeds do not represent their posterior distribution.

No source-population replay is available. Target-table source-statistic comparisons are unavailable even when a margin was used as a construction anchor. Analytic checks concern the explicitly specified law, not a reconstructed source population or target validation.

Implementation samples the stated laws without clipping or rescaling realized tables. If floating-point RNG output is nonfinite or outside declared open support, execution fails explicitly. Finite successful output is not the proof of population moments; the analytic law supplies that proof.

design.derivation: Exact task quotas and support; not the source demographic distribution.

age_law.derivation: Uniform integer allocation within each task band is a completion assumption.

dependence_law.derivation: Factorized joint law with no admitted dependence constraints. Zero population projections are consequences, not tuning goals.

bmi.derivation: k=(26.5/4.1)^2 and theta=4.1^2/26.5, giving gamma mean k*theta and variance k*theta^2.

glucose.derivation: Single source mean/SD pair 5.1,0.5 multiplied by fixed protocol 18.0 gives 91.8,9.0. With L=126 and p=91.8/L, concentration c=p*(1-p)/(9.0/L)^2-1; alpha=p*c; beta=(1-p)*c. Original/converted values are one evidence pair.

hba1c.derivation: Use published percent row once. With L=100 and p=5.6/L, c=p*(1-p)/(0.3/L)^2-1; alpha=p*c; beta=(1-p)*c.

parameter_uncertainty.derivation: No unsupported estimator precision or source-independent replication is introduced.
